uncited: This method optimizes the hybrid implicit isosurface extraction process by replacing octants with dual cells in non-boundary (same-level) regions, significantly reducing the number of primitives traversed during ray tracing.

It achieves an approximate 4× speedup in extraction time by leveraging the fact that an octant of a cell remains an octant of the corresponding dual cell, ensuring the final isosurface geometry is unchanged when eight octants are merged into a single dual cell.

It builds on [Hybrid Implicit Isosurface Ray Tracing](3832-hybrid-implicit-isosurface-ray-tracing.md) and is distinct from [Active Cell Filtering](9505-active-cell-filtering.md), which filters input cells before primitive generation.
- **Cell $C_i$**: The input volume element.
- **Octant $O_{ij}$**: One of eight sub-cubes of $C_i$, indexed by $j \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$.
Vertices require reconstruction via the GTI method if at a boundary.
- **Dual Cell $D_{ij}$**: A cell enclosed by data points of known values.
Its vertices are data points, requiring no reconstruction kernel.
The center of $C_i$ is a vertex of $D_{ij}$.
Iterate through each input cell $C_i$ in the input mesh.
Construct the candidate dual cell $D_{ij}$ using `findDualCell(Ci, j)`.
Determine if $D_{ij}$ lies in a same-level region using `isDualCellInSameLevel(Dij)`.
Check if the isovalue lies within the value range of $D_{ij}$ using `Dij.ValueRange().Contains(isovalue)`.
If true, and if $j=7$ (to avoid duplicate insertion for shared dual cells), insert $D_{ij}$ into `res`.
Initialize the octant $O_{ij}$ using `initOctant(Ci, j)`.
Compute vertex values for $O_{ij}$ using the GTI method.
Check if the isovalue lies within the value range of $O_{ij}$.
- **TB-AMR vs BS-AMR**: For BS-AMR (Brick-Based), cells are stored in uniform grids, making same-level checks trivial.
For TB-AMR, cells are stored in an octree, and neighboring cell levels are not readily available.
- **Duplicate Insertion**: The condition `j == 7` prevents inserting the same dual cell multiple times when it is shared by adjacent parent cells.
At level boundaries, octants must still be used with GTI reconstruction, which is more costly.
While similar optimizations were applied to BS-AMR data in previous work [WWW∗19], the TB-AMR implementation required additional complexity due to the octree data layout.
The method is part of the hybrid implicit isosurface rendering pipeline integrated into OSPRay.
